title: A Flang Plugin for Fortran Feature Characterization
problem: Compiler developers must manually query software experts to identify which Fortran language features are critical for new hardware systems, a process that is time-consuming and error-prone. Automating this feature detection would enable faster compiler development for leading-edge systems.
motivation: Automated feature characterization helps compiler developers prioritize implementation effort to get important scientific and HPC applications running on new compute systems without extensive manual profiling.
method: The authors develop a Flang compiler plugin that analyzes the parse tree representation generated by the Fortran frontend for LLVM. The plugin detects key Fortran features by traversing parse tree nodes corresponding to features of interest. They validate the tool on four applications, three manually profiled by experts, comparing automated results against manual characterizations and generating new characterizations.
key_novelty: Automated detection of Fortran language feature usage through parse tree analysis, replacing manual expert profiling for compiler development prioritization.
contributions: A Flang compiler plugin for automated Fortran feature detection from parse trees
Validation methodology comparing automated detection against manual expert characterization
Intent to open-source the tool for community contribution and extension

metrics.accuracy: Feature detection accuracy validated against manual expert profiling

limitations: Limitations of feature detection accuracy and feature coverage are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Automated Fortran language feature characterization for compiler development
